history.author: Mark Tyson
history.titleZh: Ambitious gamer turns fanless Subway menu PCs into gaming rigs — passive Intel Core i3 units manage just 15 fps in GTA V and 25 fps in Minecraft
history.descriptionZh:
一位名为Garkus的科技博主近日在YouTube上发布了一段有趣的视频：他找来三台曾长期在赛百味（Subway）餐厅收银台后方服役、用于展示三明治菜单的数字标牌迷你PC，试图将它们改造成游戏电脑。这些电脑采用了英特尔Skylake时代的Core i3-6100U处理器，已经连续运行了约十年，本应被当作电子垃圾处理，但Garkus与配套的LG商用显示器一起将它们救了下来，并展开了一系列“复古改造”实验。

从硬件规格来看，这三台迷你PC均为研华（Advantech）DS-081型号，具体子型号为DS-081GB-U21A1E。其处理器为双核四线程的Core i3-6100U，基准频率2.3 GHz，TDP在7.5W至15W之间可配置，性能放在今天显然已相当落后。集成显卡为Intel HD Graphics 520，拥有24个执行单元（EU），最高频率仅1.0 GHz，且需要共享系统内存作为显存。此外，机器原本只配备了4GB DDR4内存（占用一个插槽）和一块64GB SATA SSD。尽管身材小巧且完全被动散热，DS-081在扩展性上却出乎意料地丰富：机身外部提供了两个HDMI 1.4接口、双千兆以太网口、四个USB 3.0接口、音频输入输出以及一个RS-232串口；内部则拥有两条DDR4-2133 SODIMM内存插槽（最大支持32GB）、一个SATA III硬盘位和一个看似M.2 2242形状的mSATA接口。该设备被设计用于在0至40摄氏度的环境温度下7×24小时不间断运行数字标牌任务。

在改造过程中，Garkus发现这些电脑启动后直接进入Windows的Kiosk模式并自动显示赛百味菜单。他为测试机添加了一根4GB DDR4内存，使总容量提升至8GB。经过一番系统安装上的折腾，他最终将三台机器分别配置为：一台保留Windows 10，一台安装Bazzite Linux（因为SteamOS拒绝在仅有SATA存储的机器上安装），第三台则黑苹果安装了macOS Monterey。

随后的游戏测试结果并不意外。首先运行的“极品飞车”级轻量游戏《宝石迷阵》（Peggle）毫无压力，因为这是一款2D解谜游戏。但随后Garkus直接跳到了《侠盗猎车手V》（GTA V）。这款经典旧作在默认高画质下仅能跑出约15帧/秒的帧率，而且在Bazzite系统上启动耗时极长，退出时还会崩溃。由于GTA V在编译着色器时占用资源，Garkus甚至趁此机会开始测试《马里奥赛车Wii》的模拟性能，显然这种行为并不符合正规基准测试流程。接下来他在《我的世界》中的测试给出了大约25帧/秒但极度不稳定的表现，且视频中并未公开分辨率与画质设置的具体参数。

最终结论毫无悬念：这些前数字标牌迷你PC在2026年完全无法胜任主流3A游戏，甚至经过内存扩容也难以改善。Garkus认为，它们最适合的用途是模拟老式游戏主机，大致覆盖到PlayStation 2和初代Xbox这一代。但基于其硬件性能，即便使用PS2模拟器，也需要选择负载较轻的游戏并调低设置才能获得流畅体验。这则新闻既展示了低功耗嵌入式硬件在生命周期结束后的另一种可能，也生动说明性能冗余对于新用途的决定性作用。对于追求小型化、低功耗和静音体验的玩家而言，这类设备可以作为复古模拟器或轻量流媒体盒子，但绝非现代游戏的理想平台。

history.title: Startup plans to put nuclear-powered data centers in the sea — modular units could be much faster to deploy, but questions about reliability and longevity remain
history.description: Atomarine wants to put data centers on modular barges for ocean-based deployments. The firm says these can be powered by LNG-powered ships and seamlessly swap to ship-based SMRs when they become available.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Data centers on land are facing increasing opposition and having a hard time getting off the ground — from power connection issues that can take months or years to resolve, to neighborhood concerns about noise and air pollution, as well as their impact on the local water supply. One startup called Atomarine wants to solve this by building nuclear-powered data centers on barges and deploying them at sea.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)Photonics and high-speed data movement is the next big AI bottleneckThe data center cooling state of playMassive AI data center buildouts are squeezing energy suppliesUltra Ethernet: The data center interconnection of tomorrowThere have already been various proposals to put data centers out at sea (or even submerged) from established names and startups. We’ve seen conventional examples from companies like Samsung Heavy Industries and Japanese shipping company MOL who to put the servers on dedicated ships and are powered by liquefied natural gas (LNG). There are also more innovative solutions from startups that want to put them in the bases of ocean-based wind turbines or in wave energy converters.Atomarine differs by building data centers as floating barges, similar to floating oil platforms, which can be deployed anywhere — even in international waters. This should help cut down on the permitting process, and it doesn’t have to worry about disturbing neighbors. The electricity needed to run the infrastructure is then delivered by a power ship moored alongside the barge supplied by LNG ships. Once small modular nuclear reactors (SMRs) become commercially available and certified for shipboard use, operators can then swap out the conventionally powered electricity suppliers with a nuclear one relatively quickly. And because these data center barges are modular in nature, it would be relatively easy to upgrade and scale the floating data center.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While this project sounds promising, building a megastructure like this comes with several challenges. The biggest one is that the ocean is massive and unpredictable, so these barges must be engineered to face extreme weather conditions, making them quite expensive to deploy. It must also be connected to high-speed internet (unless the operators plan to ship tons of drives daily), so they’ll have to lay undersea cables, as well. Furthermore, data servers are particularly sensitive equipment, so they must be upgraded to ensure that they can withstand the continuous rolling motion and the salty environment of the sea. There’s also the question of an SMR’s viability in shipborne use, although the U.S. Navy already has a good track record of running nuclear reactors aboard massive vessels.The mounting opposition against data centers, both by the general public and politicians, is making it harder and more time-consuming to build new projects across the U.S. While an ocean-based data center like this is likely going to be significantly more expensive and technically challenging than land-based developments, this might become the fastest option in the future if the idea proves to be viable. history.author: Jowi Morales
history.titleZh: Startup plans to put nuclear-powered data centers in the sea — modular units could be much faster to deploy, but questions about reliability and longevity remain
history.descriptionZh:
随着人工智能对算力需求的爆发式增长，陆地数据中心的建设正面临前所未有的阻力。从需要数月甚至数年才能解决的电力并网问题，到周边社区对噪音、空气污染以及水资源消耗的担忧，传统数据中心项目在美国越来越难以落地。针对这一困境，初创公司Atomarine提出了一种颠覆性构想：将核能数据中心建在大型驳船之上，部署到海上，从而绕开陆地上的种种限制。

事实上，将数据中心移向海洋并非全新概念。此前已有多种方案，例如韩国三星重工和日本航运公司商船三井（MOL）曾提出使用专用船舶搭载服务器，并以液化天然气（LNG）为动力；也有初创企业尝试将数据中心集成到海上风力涡轮机的基础平台或波浪能转换装置中。Atomarine的不同之处在于，它采用类似海上石油平台的浮动驳船设计，这些驳船可以部署在任意海域，甚至包括国际公海。这种方式不仅大幅减少了行政审批环节，也彻底避免了与陆地居民的纠纷。数据中心的电力由停靠在旁侧的专用电力船提供，该电力船依靠LNG运输船补给燃料。一旦小型模块化核反应堆（SMR）实现商业化并获得船载使用认证，运营商就能较快地将常规能源供电系统替换为核动力模块。同时，由于驳船采用模块化架构，未来升级和扩展计算能力也相对便捷。

当然，这一宏伟构想也伴随着显著的技术挑战。首先，海洋环境广阔且难以预测，驳船必须为抵御极端天气而进行高强度工程设计，这导致部署成本极为高昂。其次，数据中心必须接入高速互联网，除非运营方打算每天用船只运送大量硬盘，否则就必须铺设海底光缆。此外，服务器是高度精密的设备，必须针对船舶的持续颠簸和海洋盐雾腐蚀环境进行专门加固。至于小型模块化核反应堆在船载环境中的实际可行性，虽然仍需验证，但美国海军在大型舰艇上运行核反应堆已有长期成功经验。

目前，公众和政界对数据中心的反对声浪正使美国新项目的审批与建设变得越来越艰难、耗时。尽管海上数据中心在成本和工程复杂度上很可能远超陆地设施，但如果这一方案最终被证明可行，它或许会成为未来算力扩张的最快捷路径。Tom's Hardware也将持续关注相关技术进展，包括光子学高速数据传输、数据中心冷却技术、能源供应瓶颈以及下一代超以太网互连等前沿话题。

history.titleZh: Tim Cook hints at iCloud Plus tier for AI power users
history.descriptionZh:
苹果公司正在考虑允许用户通过付费方式提升其人工智能功能的使用上限。在周四的财报电话会议上，苹果首席执行官蒂姆·库克表示，他相信人们会“大量”使用Apple Intelligence和即将推出的Siri AI，并透露“我们将在iCloud Plus上提供某种升级选项，让用户可以购买更高的配额。”这一表态意味着，苹果可能正在为重度AI用户设计新的付费层级。

今年秋季，苹果将随iOS 27正式推出屡次延期的新版Siri AI。该功能能够回答关于当前屏幕内容的问题，并跨应用执行操作，同时还包含一款独立的全新Siri AI应用，提供类似ChatGPT的聊天界面。苹果在六月份曾表示，包括图像生成在内的AI功能“因依赖强大的服务器模型，设有每日使用限制”，并称“大多数iCloud Plus套餐已提供更高访问权限”。不过现在看来，苹果计划为那些打算频繁使用AI功能的用户增设额外付费档位。

在最新财报中，苹果过去几个月的服务业务（包括iCloud Plus、Apple TV和Apple One等订阅服务）收入达到307.4亿美元。此举若落地，将有助于苹果进一步挖掘AI功能带来的服务收入增长潜力。

history.content: I am not by any means an expert at finance but I think I do now have some advice for people who are: Do not name your hedge fund anything that will be hilarious if it blows up. Don’t use a name like “Long-Term Capital Management” or “Amaranth Advisors” (named for the floral symbol for immortality). Certainly do not call yourself “Situational Awareness,” which might as well just be “Hubris, Inc.”Anyway, Situational Awareness, the hedge fund started by a 24-year-old former OpenAI employee that focuses on artificial intelligence bets, has sold most or all, depending on who’s reporting, of its entire public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel after several bad weeks for AI stocks, and that’s the situation we are all now aware of. You may recall earlier this week I noted the market had gotten particularly nervous about AI risk; as it turns out, we have discovered one firm that was swimming without a bathing suit.How bad is it? Well, according to CNBC, the fund was worth $45 billion at the start of July. It is now worth $10 billion, after the sale of assets to Griffin. The previous record holder on all-time trading losses was Archegos Capital Management, which lost $8 billion in 10 days in 2021, according to The Wall Street Journal. If these numbers hold, Situational Awareness’ AI bets lost three times as much.Every detail of this disaster is funnier than the last. Situational Awareness had a staff of eight, of whom four were investment professionals. “The fund’s largest holdings at the end of the first quarter included Nebius Group, Sandisk, Micron and CoreWeave, according to filings,” CNBC wrote. “All four of those stocks are down more than 35 percent this month.” I expect we will hear more in the coming days, especially from the Wall Street professionals who were on the other side of these jokers’ trades.“Basically, this investment firm will be kind of like a brain trust on AI.”How did we get here? Situational Awareness LP was named for a series of facile essays about machine intelligence published by the improbably named Leopold Aschenbrenner, the 24-year-old mastermind of the hedge fund. “We are building machines that can think and reason,” he writes, betraying that he has no idea what thinking could possibly mean. “By 2025/26, these machines will outpace many college graduates. By the end of the decade, they will be smarter than you or I; we will have superintelligence, in the true sense of the word. Along the way, national security forces not seen in half a century will be unleashed, and before long, The Project will be on. If we’re lucky, we’ll be in an all-out race with the CCP; if we’re unlucky, an all-out war.”There is a part of me that wants to go line by line to dunk on every claim here, beginning with the very first sentence, “You can see the future first in San Francisco,” but I am going to stifle the impulse. The essays are the theoretical underpinnings of the hedge fund. The upshot is that artificial general intelligence is real (lol) and will arrive in 2027 (lmao). So the entire point of the hedge fund was to dump as much money as possible into AI stocks and then get very, very rich.“Basically, this investment firm will be kind of like a brain trust on AI,” Aschenbrenner told Dwarkesh Patel in a four-hour podcast interview, the preferred intellectual medium of the Silicon Valley elite. “We’re going to have way more situational awareness than any of the people who manage money in New York. We’re definitely going to do great on investing, but it’s the same sort of situational awareness that is going to be important for understanding what’s happening, being a voice of reason publicly, and being able to be in a position to advise.”I really cannot begin to explain how much this essay’s bad graphs impressed A Certain Kind of Silicon Valley Guy. Axios wrote breathlessly about the essay that “his opus is a useful, eye-opening synthesis of high-level Silicon Valley conversations.” Aschenbrenner’s insights “expanded my perspective as an AI practitioner beyond just the technical aspects,” wrote Shav Vimalendiran, a cofounder of SAMMY Labs, an AI company that is meant to simplify legal statutes. You know who else liked it? Ivanka Trump, who called it “an excellent and important read.”Why would these purportedly serious people buy in on a 24-year-old’s very first hedge fund?Situational Awareness’ backers included Patrick and John Collison, who cofounded Stripe, and two Meta AI leaders, Daniel Gross and Nat Friedman. The fund’s director of research was Carl Shulman, who’d worked at Peter Thiel’s Clarium Capital. Eventually, Jane Street — the Wall Street firm budding young Effective Altruists, including Sam Bankman-Fried, join — bought in too. “Jane Street’s investment in Situational Awareness is particularly notable because the firm rarely allocates capital to outside money managers,” The Wall Street Journal wrote in June.Why would these purportedly serious people buy in on a 24-year-old’s very first hedge fund? My best guess is that Aschenbrenner’s investors were relying on the social bona fides he had cultivated. Social proof is the laziest and most disastrous way to vet people — ask any Theranos investor, or for that matter, anyone who had Bernie Madoff managing their money — but I suppose it’s good enough for Silicon Valley.At age 17, Aschenbrenner was called “an economics prodigy” by Tyler Cowen, a libertarian economist famous in certain Silicon Valley circles. Cowen’s Emergent Ventures even gave him a grant, according to Fortune. Aschenbrenner published essays in Works in Progress, a publication funded by Stripe. During his time at Columbia University, Aschenbrenner cofounded the college’s Effective Altruism chapter. After graduating in 2021 as Columbia University’s valedictorian at age 19, Aschenbrenner went on to work at the FTX Future Fund, the philanthropic arm of cryptocurrency exchange FTX, which collapsed after Sam Bankman-Fried’s fraud was revealed. Among his coworkers at the fund were William MacAskill, the philosopher-king of the Effective Altruism movement, and Avital Balwit, who would later become the chief of staff at Anthropic.From there, he immediately got a job on OpenAI’s superalignment team. Fortune quotes several former coworkers who describe him as being “politically clumsy,” arrogant, and abrasive. “Multiple researchers also described a holiday party where, in a casual group discussion, Aschenbrenner told then Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang how many GPUs OpenAI had—‘just straight out in the open,’ as one put it,” wrote Fortune’s Sharon Goldman in her profile. (Both Wang and Aschenbrenner deny this occurred.) Aschenbrenner was later fired from OpenAI for leaking internal information in an incident unrelated to the Scale AI thing. Two months after that, Aschenbrenner published Situational Awareness, his essays.“Obviously, not blowing up is task number one and two.”Now astute readers may notice that Aschenbrenner had no previous money management experience on his resume when he launched his hedge fund. They may also notice that the sum total of Aschenbrenner’s work experience was a few months at FTX and about a year at OpenAI. They may wonder if this means that the Collisons, Gross, and Friedman have too much money to burn if they are funding this little shit. (Yes, obviously. Tax the rich!)Here’s how Aschenbrenner described the fund’s strategy back in the halcyon days of 2024: “Obviously, not blowing up is task number one and two,” he told Patel. “You have to get the timing right. The sequence of bets on the way to AGI is actually pretty critical. People underrate it.”We’ll get a more complete picture of how Situational Awareness crashed and burned in the coming days, but right now it looks like this. Hedge funds often borrow money to maximize their bets. So if you really believe AI is the future, “you won’t put 100% of your money (and your investors’ money) into the AI boom,” writes Bloomberg’s Matt Levine. “You’ll put, like, 300% of your money into the AI boom.” At one point, the hedge fund claimed to be up 439 percent.The same borrowing that magnifies your wins also magnifies your losses. If you have borrowed money to bet on AI stocks, and those stocks go down — as they have done recently — the people you borrowed from will do what’s called a “margin call” and ask you to top up your loan collateral. First, Situational Awareness held calls with its investors and lenders to raise more capital, The Financial Times reported yesterday. It even offered some investors the opportunity to buy parts of its portfolio. This morning, Situational Awareness sold what the FT said was “a large portion of its $16bn public equity” to Citadel, Griffin’s hedge fund.“You’ve got to be really, really careful about your overall risk positioning.”Public equity is the most liquid part of anyone’s portfolio. Situational Awareness still has private holdings, including $5 billion in Anthropic, the FT reported. According to CNBC, Situational Awareness was also negotiating to sell that stake, “but it wasn’t clear if that deal was done.”“You’ve got to be really, really careful about your overall risk positioning,” Aschenbrenner said in 2024. “If you expect these crazy events to play out, there’s going to be crazy things you didn’t foresee.” One of those things, perhaps, is that artificial general intelligence isn’t coming — or at least, not by 2027. “A friend joked that the investment firm is perfectly hedged for me,” Aschenbrenner said. “Either AGI happens this decade and my human capital depreciates, but I turn it into financial capital, or no AGI happens and the firm doesn’t do well, but I’m still in my twenties and smart.”Yes, Aschenbrenner is certainly in his 20s!
history.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
history.descriptionZh:
一家由24岁前OpenAI员工创办、名为“Situational Awareness”（情境感知）的人工智能对冲基金，在经历数周AI股票大跌后，已将几乎全部公开股票投资组合出售给肯·格里芬的城堡 Citadel 对冲基金。该基金曾以极度乐观的AI信仰著称，如今却成为史上最大单笔交易亏损的案例——其亏损规模甚至超过2021年Archegos Capital Management创下的80亿美元纪录。

基金规模从7月初的450亿美元暴跌至100亿美元，仅AI押注就损失了约350亿美元。其重仓股包括Nebius Group、Sandisk、Micron和CoreWeave，这四只股票本月均下跌超35%。基金只有8名员工，其中4人是投资专业人士，却管理着巨额资金。创始人利奥波德·阿申布伦纳（Leopold Aschenbrenner）年仅24岁，此前没有丝毫资金管理经验——他的职业生涯只有几个月在FTX Future Fund和约一年在OpenAI超级对齐团队的经历。他曾因泄露内部信息被OpenAI解雇，随后在2024年发表了名为《情境感知》的系列文章，预言“机器将在2025/26年超越多数大学毕业生，到2020年代末将拥有真正意义上的超级智能”，并声称“人工智能通用智能将在2027年到来”。正是这套极具煽动性的理论吸引了众多硅谷大佬投资：Stripe联合创始人Patrick和John Collison、Meta AI领袖Daniel Gross和Nat Friedman、以及Jane Street等机构都重金押注。基金经理沙尔·舒尔曼曾在彼得·蒂尔的Clarium Capital工作。

阿申布伦纳当时宣称：“显然，不爆仓是第一和第二要务。你必须把握好时机。通往AGI的bet序列非常关键。”他计划利用杠杆尽可能多地押注AI股票，基金一度声称回报率达439%。然而杠杆是双向的。当AI股票下跌时，贷方发出追加保证金通知，基金不得不召开会议筹集资金，甚至向投资者出售投资组合股份，最终被迫将160亿美元公共股权中的大部分卖给城堡基金。据英国《金融时报》报道，该基金还持有50亿美元的Anthropic私人股份，正在谈判出售但尚不确定交易是否完成。

阿申布伦纳曾告诉记者：“你必须非常非常小心整体风险定位。如果你预期这些疯狂的事情会发生，就会有你没预见到疯狂的事情。”他显然没有预见到自己会成为这场AI狂热中最具讽刺意味的牺牲品。他曾自我安慰说：“朋友开玩笑说这家投资公司对我完美对冲——如果AGI在本十年成真，我的人力资本贬值但转化为金融资本；如果AGI没来，公司表现不好，但我才二十多岁还很聪明。”如今，他确实还在二十多岁，但他的基金已经爆仓了。

这场灾难揭示了硅谷精英圈层中的危险现象：社会信誉被当成投资能力的证明。阿申布伦纳17岁时被自由意志主义经济学家泰勒·考恩称为“经济学神童”，获得考恩的Emergent Ventures资助，在Stripe资助的刊物上发表文章，在哥伦比亚大学担任毕业生代表并以19岁毕业，参与创办有效利他主义社团，在FTX工作过。这些履历让投资者们盲目相信了一个毫无投资经验的年轻人对AI的狂热预言，而忽略了最朴素的常识——就像Theranos投资者和麦道夫受害者一样，他们被“社会证明”所欺骗。

目前尚不清楚基金的全部损失细节，但已经可以确认这是金融史上最惨烈的AI押注之一。整个事件提醒人们：当24岁的前OpenAI员工以“情境感知”为名创立的基金，实际上最缺乏的正是情境感知——他们既没有感知到AI泡沫的破裂风险，也没有感知到自己正在用杠杆重演金融史上前人的悲剧。
